chunks: Abu al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Ahmad al-Tabari narrated to us, he said: Abu Sa'id narrated to us, he said: Karrash narrated to us, he said: My master Anas ibn Malik narrated to us, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
For the fasting person are two joys: a joy at the time of breaking his fast, and a joy on the day he meets his Lord.

He means by his joy at breaking his fast the joy of the Muslim in securing that day in the register of his good deeds and the surplus of his actions, not that his joy is in what was permitted of food at that time.

That is so, and joy in eating and the need of the belly from the finest things by which the righteous are praised is not [the primary joy]; as for his joy at meeting his Lord, Exalted and Glorified, it is by what Allah pours upon him from the bounty of His gift, which no one from the people of the Resurrection has like it, except for one who did like his deed.
ai.seo_question: What are the two joys of a fasting person according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq clarifies that the first joy is spiritual—rejoicing in the accumulation of good deeds rather than mere physical satiety—while the second, superior joy is the divine reward on the Day of Judgment. This distinction highlights the Shia emphasis on the metaphysical value of worship over its physical aspects, framing fasting as a means of spiritual elevation and ultimate divine proximity.
